temps.title: Air & Sea Temp (ONI)
temps.plain: The ocean surface in the Pacific is significantly warmer than average. This massive pool of heat warms the air above it, changing global weather patterns.
temps.tech: The Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) measures 3-month rolling average SST anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region (5°N-5°S, 120°-170°W). Current anomaly is +2.1°C, indicating a strong El Niño episode driving enhanced equatorial convection.

pressure.title: Atmospheric Pressure (SOI)
pressure.plain: The normal pressure system over the Pacific is reversed. High pressure over Australia causes droughts, while low pressure over Tahiti brings rain.
pressure.tech: The Southern Oscillation Index (SOI) is -1.8, tracking the standardized sea level pressure difference between Tahiti and Darwin. Negative values signify anomalously weak trade winds and El Niño conditions.

thermocline.title: Thermocline Depth
thermocline.plain: The boundary between warm surface water and cold deep water has flattened out, trapping heat at the surface.
thermocline.tech: The equatorial Pacific thermocline (measured at the 20°C isotherm) slope has flattened. Downwelling in the East Pacific suppresses nutrient-rich cold upwelling, deepening the mixed layer.

kelvin.title: Kelvin Waves
kelvin.plain: Massive underwater waves of warm water are traveling from Indonesia towards South America, fueling the El Niño event.
kelvin.tech: Downwelling equatorial Kelvin waves, triggered by westerly wind bursts, are propagating eastward across the Pacific basin, transporting immense anomalous oceanic heat content to the eastern boundary.

winds.title: Trade Winds
winds.plain: The winds that normally blow west across the Pacific have weakened or even reversed, allowing warm water to slosh back east.
winds.tech: Low-level equatorial easterlies have anomalously weakened or reversed into Westerly Wind Bursts (WWBs). This reduces Ekman transport and equatorial upwelling.

walker.title: Walker Circulation
walker.plain: The massive air loop over the Pacific has shifted. Storms and rising air have moved from Indonesia out to the middle of the ocean.
walker.tech: The Walker Circulation has shifted eastward. Anomalous ascending motion (convection) is centered over the central/eastern Pacific, with anomalous descending motion (subsidence) over the Maritime Continent.

transport.title: Overturning Transport
transport.plain: The massive ocean current that brings warm water north is slowing down significantly.
transport.tech: Meridional volume transport is measured at 12.4 Sverdrups (1 Sv = 10^6 m^3/s), representing a statistically significant weakening trend in the Atlantic overturning circulation.

blob.title: Subpolar Gyre SST
blob.plain: A mysterious cold patch in the North Atlantic indicates that warm water is not reaching as far north as it used to.
blob.tech: The North Atlantic Warming Hole (Cold Blob) exhibits an anomaly of -2.1°C, a classic fingerprint of AMOC slowdown due to reduced northward oceanic heat advection.

salinity.title: Surface Salinity
salinity.plain: Melting ice is making the ocean surface fresher. Fresh water is lighter than salty water, so it does not sink easily, jamming up the ocean currents.
salinity.tech: Surface salinity anomalies in the Labrador and Irminger Seas (34.2 PSU) show enhanced freshening due to Greenland ice sheet meltwater fluxes, increasing stratification and suppressing deep water formation.

gulfstream.title: Gulf Stream Velocity
gulfstream.plain: The famous Gulf Stream current is moving slower than normal.
gulfstream.tech: Geostrophic velocities derived from satellite altimetry show a reduction in Gulf Stream core speed (0.9 m/s), consistent with weakened western boundary current dynamics.

convection.title: Convection Depth
convection.plain: Water is not sinking as deep as it should in the North Atlantic, slowing the entire global conveyor belt.
convection.tech: Wintertime deep convection depth in the subpolar North Atlantic is anomalously shallow (850 m), indicating reduced North Atlantic Deep Water (NADW) formation.

heat.title: Heat Transport
heat.plain: The ocean is carrying less heat from the equator to the poles, which could drastically cool Europe.
heat.tech: Meridional Oceanic Heat Transport (MHT) across 26.5°N is estimated at 1.10 Petawatts (PW), showing a negative anomaly linked to the weakened overturning volume.

winds.title: 10 hPa Winds
winds.plain: The high-altitude winds spinning around the North Pole have actually reversed direction from west-to-east, to east-to-west.
winds.tech: Zonal-mean zonal winds at 60°N and 10 hPa have reversed to -2.0 m/s, strictly defining a Sudden Stratospheric Warming (SSW) event.

ao.title: Arctic Oscillation
ao.plain: The boundary keeping cold Arctic air trapped up north has weakened, allowing freezing air to spill south.
ao.tech: The Arctic Oscillation (AO) index is strongly negative (-1.48), indicating high geopotential heights in the Arctic and a weakened, meandering tropospheric jet stream.

structure.title: Vortex Structure
structure.plain: The main spinning pool of cold air has split into two separate, smaller spinning pools.
structure.tech: Geopotential height fields indicate a Wave-2 perturbation, resulting in a complete barotropic splitting of the stratospheric polar vortex into sister vortices over Canada and Eurasia.

temp.title: Stratospheric Temp
temp.plain: The air way up high over the Arctic has suddenly become much hotter than normal.
temp.tech: A rapid adiabatic heating event (+10°C anomaly) has occurred in the polar stratosphere over a few days, driven by planetary wave breaking and anomalous downwelling.

nao.title: North Atlantic Oscillation
nao.plain: Pressure patterns over the Atlantic are pushing Arctic storms directly into Europe and the US East Coast.
nao.tech: A negative NAO index (-2.10) indicates a weakened Icelandic Low and Azores High, driving anomalous easterly flow and severe winter conditions into mid-latitudes.

ozone.title: Stratospheric Ozone
ozone.plain: Ozone levels have changed because the cold air that normally destroys ozone has moved away.
ozone.tech: Anomalous transport dynamics associated with the SSW have led to localized surges in column ozone, as the lack of Polar Stratospheric Clouds (PSCs) halts ozone depletion mechanisms.

atl.title: Atlantic Basin Outlook & ACE
atl.plain: The Atlantic basin has experienced an unusually quiet season due to strong vertical wind shear and dry air suppression driven by El Niño.
atl.tech: Active shear anomalies (>25 kts) across the Main Development Region (MDR) have significantly disrupted tropical cyclogenesis throughout the late season.

pac.title: Eastern Pacific Basin & Pressure
pac.plain: The Eastern Pacific has sustained localized activity, supported by anomalously high sea surface temperatures exceeding 28.5°C.
pac.tech: Minimum central pressure gradient drives the cyclostrophic wind balance. Rapid deepening is defined as a pressure drop of >= 24 hPa in 24 hours.

gulf.title: Gulf of Mexico Loop Current & Surge
gulf.plain: Shallow bathymetry and high water temperatures in the Gulf amplify storm surge heights dramatically during landfall.
gulf.tech: Upper Ocean Heat Content (UOHC) in the Gulf remains above 60 kJ/cm², maintaining high potential intensity parameters for incoming disturbances.

shear.title: Vertical Wind Shear & ACE
shear.plain: Strong winds high up in the atmosphere are shearing the tops off developing storms, preventing them from organizing.
shear.tech: Tropospheric vertical wind shear vector magnitude between 200hPa and 850hPa exceeds 30 knots across key subtropical development corridors.

popocatepetl.title: Popocatépetl (Mexico)
popocatepetl.plain: Continuous degassing with frequent ash plumes reaching 22,000 feet and incandescent ballistic ejecta near the crater rim.
popocatepetl.tech: SO2 flux exceeds 3,200 t/day paired with sustained harmonic tremor bursts (2-4 Hz) indicating magma ascent in the upper conduit.

etna.title: Mount Etna (Italy)
etna.plain: Strombolian explosions and episodic lava fountaining from the Southeast Crater.
etna.tech: Infrasound acoustic pressure spikes and elevated volcanic tremor amplitude linked to volatile-rich basaltic magma recharge.
